2) Audit / logs:

From: dev_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Architecture deep-dive — preliminary answers + attachments

Alex / team — thanks for the list, this is helpful. Quick, high-level responses and I've attached the draft agenda + diagram we plan to walk through. We'll expand these during the call.

1) KMS / encryption: we support per-customer KMS integrations for Private deployments and Dedicated (via customer-managed KMS in Cloud Provider). We emit key-rotation events and can provide key usage logs as part of SOC 2 artifact bundles.

2) Audit / logs: we provide request-level request_ids, timestamps, route/model, and token-count metadata in our audit logs. Retention is configurable; default 90 days, enterprise buckets available for longer retention.

3) Autoscaling / failover: Dedicated autoscaling policies are policy-driven (min/max pool size, queue settings). Burst capacity is a separate pool with defined SLAs; routing fallback will use a policy you opt into (e.g., route to quantized variant or hosted fallback). Cold-starts for large models can range from ~2–10s depending on quantization and instance type; we discuss warm-pool strategies in the agenda.

4) KV cache: continuous batching + prefix/KV cache are orthogonal; cache eviction is LRU per-shard with TTL which you can tune. Hit rates depend on workload locality; we'll show dashboard examples.

5) Tokenization parity: custom tokenizers are supported; embedding parity requires the same tokenizer and any special pre/post-processing be included in the repro bundle. We'll cover best practices for embeddings and reranking tests.

6) Networking: we'll share a recommended VPC peering layout (attached) and a short list of egress/port rules.

Attachments: agenda_arch_review_v1.pdf, network_diagram_v1.png, redwood-datasheet.pdf

I'll push a Google Drive folder with materials here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_arch_review

See you on Tue 03/02 — I'll join the call 10 minutes early to validate any screen-sharing needs.

—Dev
